scenes.title: Overview
scenes.caption: Over 150,000 people visit the shrine every day for worship, being one of the most visited religious sites in the world.
scenes.quote: Over 150,000 people visit the shrine every day for worship, being one of the most visited religious sites in the world.

scenes.title: Overview
scenes.caption: The pool on the site of the gurdwara was completed by the fourth Sikh Guru, Guru Ram Das, in 1577.
scenes.quote: The pool on the site of the gurdwara was completed by the fourth Sikh Guru, Guru Ram Das, in 1577.

scenes.title: Overview
scenes.caption: In 1604, Guru Arjan, the fifth Sikh Guru, placed a copy of the Adi Granth in the Golden Temple and played a prominent role in its development.
scenes.quote: In 1604, Guru Arjan, the fifth Sikh Guru, placed a copy of the Adi Granth in the Golden Temple and played a prominent role in its development.

scenes.title: Overview
scenes.caption: Maharaja Ranjit Singh, after founding the Sikh Empire, rebuilt it in marble and copper in 1809, and overlaid the sanctum with gold leaf in 1830.
scenes.quote: Maharaja Ranjit Singh, after founding the Sikh Empire, rebuilt it in marble and copper in 1809, and overlaid the sanctum with gold leaf in 1830.

scenes.title: Overview
scenes.caption: It became a centre of the Singh Sabha Movement between 1883 and the 1920s, and the Punjabi Suba Movement between 1947 and 1966.
scenes.quote: It became a centre of the Singh Sabha Movement between 1883 and the 1920s, and the Punjabi Suba Movement between 1947 and 1966.

scenes.title: Overview
scenes.caption: In 1984, Prime Minister Indira Gandhi sent in the Indian Army as part of Operation Blue Star, leading to the deaths of thousands of soldiers, militants and civilians, as well as causing significant damage to the gurdwara and the destruction of the nearby Akal Takht—the prime seat of authority for the Sikhs.
